facts.text: The operating domain, called ODD in road-vehicle terminology, specifies the environmental and operating conditions under which a safety claim is intended to hold.
facts.quote: The operating domain (ODD in road-vehicle terminology) answers the question "under what environmental and operating conditions is the safety claim intended to hold?"

facts.text: An operating-domain specification lists every condition the system may meet and defines explicit in-domain and out-of-domain boundaries.
facts.quote: It lists every condition the system may meet, with explicit in-domain and out-of-domain boundaries.

facts.text: ISO 34503:2023 provides a hierarchical way to specify an operating design domain for automated road vehicles.
facts.quote: ISO 34503:2023 gives a hierarchical way to specify an ODD for automated road vehicles

facts.text: ASAM OpenODD version 1.0.0 was released on 3 April 2025.
facts.quote: ASAM OpenODD 1.0.0 (released 3 April 2025)

facts.text: ASAM OpenODD 1.0.0 provides a technology-independent data model for operating-domain taxonomies in machine-readable YAML and CSV formats, with restrictive and permissive definitions.
facts.quote: ASAM OpenODD 1.0.0 (released 3 April 2025) gives a technology-independent data model for operating-domain taxonomies in machine-readable formats (YAML, CSV) with restrictive and permissive definitions.

facts.text: ISO 34503:2023 and ASAM OpenODD 1.0.0 are useful architectural patterns for operating-domain taxonomies, but their normative scope is automated road vehicles and their default attributes are dominated by lanes and junctions.
facts.quote: Both are useful architectural patterns; their normative scope is automated road vehicles, and their default attributes (lanes, junctions) dominate.

facts.text: Off-road operating-domain taxonomies exist only as academic proposals; ODD-UM, the 2024 Springer proposal for unstructured environments, and the November 2025 agricultural ODD framework are not standards.
facts.quote: Off-road taxonomies exist only as academic proposals.

facts.text: ODD-UM, a 2022 conference paper, adapts BSI PAS 1883 and ISO 17757:2019 to underground mining.
facts.quote: ODD-UM (a 2022 conference paper) adapts BSI PAS 1883 and ISO 17757:2019 to underground mining

facts.text: A 2024 Springer paper proposes elevating operating design domain concepts for unstructured environments.
facts.quote: a 2024 Springer paper proposes elevating ODD concepts for unstructured environments

facts.text: An agricultural operating design domain framework published as an arXiv preprint in November 2025 reviews EMESRT PR-5A as an off-road ODD approach.
facts.quote: an agricultural ODD framework (arXiv preprint, November 2025) reviews EMESRT PR-5A as an off-road ODD approach.

facts.text: A proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy adapts the on-road patterns of ISO 34503 and OpenODD and the off-road patterns of ODD-UM and EMESRT; its arrangement is expert opinion.
facts.quote: A taxonomy adapted from ISO 34503 and OpenODD (on-road) and from ODD-UM and EMESRT (off-road) would have roughly these branches:

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy's site and scenery branch includes open pit, quarry face, earthworks, road construction, urban building site, underground heading, stockpile, loading pad or dig face, dump point, haul route, workshop or yard, parking, intersection, and demolition.
facts.quote: Open pit, quarry face, earthworks, road construction, urban building site, underground heading, stockpile, loading pad or dig face, dump point, haul route, workshop or yard, parking, intersection, demolition

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy's site and scenery branch also characterizes terrain roughness, slope, berms, walls, drop-offs, ruts, mud, material piles, and structures.
facts.quote: terrain roughness, slope, berms, walls, drop-offs, ruts, mud, material piles, structures

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy's machine operating state branch includes forward, reverse, turning or articulating, swing or rotation as in ISO 21815 parts 3 to 5, loaded or unloaded state, implement position, towing or trailer state, gear, speed, and acceleration.
facts.quote: Forward, reverse, turning or articulating, swing or rotation (as in the ISO 21815 parts 3 to 5), loaded or unloaded, implement position, towing or trailer state, gear, speed, acceleration

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy's machine geometry branch includes footprint, articulation angle, turning radius, swept volume, sensor height, offset, yaw and pitch, occluding machine structures, mass, and load state.
facts.quote: Footprint, articulation angle, turning radius, swept volume, sensor height, offset, yaw and pitch, occluding machine structures, mass and load state

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy's objects branch includes workers with varying posture, PPE or hi-vis presence, and partial occlusion; adult or child surrogates where applicable; light vehicles, heavy vehicles, other machines, barriers, walls, piles, rocks or boulders, attachments, and low or partially buried objects.
facts.quote: Worker (posture, PPE or hi-vis or not, partially occluded), adult or child surrogate where applicable, light vehicle, heavy vehicle, another machine, barrier, wall, pile, rock or boulder, attachment, low or partially buried object

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy characterizes objects by dimensions, pose, motion, reflectance, and material.
facts.quote: dimensions, pose, motion, reflectance or material

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy's relative interaction branch includes crossing, following, overtaking-like motion, emerging from occlusion, stationary obstacles, backing toward an object, an object approaching the machine, and an object leaving the path.
facts.quote: Crossing, following, overtaking-like motion, emerging from occlusion, stationary obstacle, backing toward an object, object approaching the machine, object leaving the path

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy's weather and air branch includes clear conditions, rain rate, snow, fog visibility, airborne dust concentration from natural sources, vehicles, blasting or excavation, spray, and mud or contamination on sensors.
facts.quote: Clear, rain rate, snow, fog visibility, airborne dust concentration (natural, vehicle-generated, blasting, excavation), spray, mud or contamination on sensors

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy's illumination branch includes solar elevation and azimuth, direct low-sun glare, shade transitions, dusk, darkness with or without site lighting, work lights, and other machines' headlights.
facts.quote: Solar elevation and azimuth, direct low-sun glare, shade transitions, dusk, darkness with or without site lighting, work lights, other machines' headlights

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy's surface and braking branch includes grade, cross-slope, loose gravel, mud, snow or ice where allowed, compaction, tyre or track state, and payload.
facts.quote: Grade, cross-slope, loose gravel, mud, snow or ice where allowed, compaction, tyre or track state, payload

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy's sensor state branch includes modality, hardware version, extrinsics, contamination, heating or cleaning status, degraded or fault state, and interference.
facts.quote: Modality, hardware version, extrinsics, contamination, heating or cleaning status, degraded or fault state, interference

facts.text: The proposed off-road operating-domain taxonomy's human and system state branch includes whether the operator has acknowledged a warning, reaction time, inhibited modes, service-brake state, latency, and network state.
facts.quote: Operator warning acknowledged or not, reaction time, inhibited modes, service-brake state, latency and network state

facts.text: The decisive design choice for off-road operating-domain coverage is to represent dimensions as attributes rather than as 100+ unrelated site labels.
facts.quote: The decisive design choice is to treat these dimensions as attributes rather than as 100+ unrelated site labels.

facts.text: Two nominally different quarries may share the same safety-relevant attributes: rough open terrain, dusty air, bright sun, high metal clutter, an 8% grade, and frequent worker and vehicle crossings.
facts.quote: Two nominally different quarries may share the same safety-relevant attributes (rough open terrain, dusty air, bright sun, high metal clutter, an 8% grade and frequent worker and vehicle crossings).

facts.text: Attribute-based operating-domain representation lets testing cover equivalence classes and interactions instead of repeating site names.
facts.quote: Attribute-based representation lets testing cover equivalence classes and interactions instead of repeating site names.
